sections.h2: What should a seller know about Paulding County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Paulding County is a fast-growing western suburb of metro Atlanta, with Dallas as the county seat and the county government campus on Constitution Boulevard. Census QuickFacts counts 190,996 residents for July 1, 2025, up 13.3 percent from the April 2020 estimates base of 168,630. That is the largest population of the four Georgia counties in this comparison, packed into 312.35 square miles of land.

The housing numbers explain why sales here move at a different pace than in rural south Georgia. The median owner-occupied home was valued at $326,300 for 2020 to 2024, and 80.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The county issued 1,326 building permits in 2025, and the median gross rent was $1,772. Workers travel a mean of 39.6 minutes to their jobs, a sign that many residents commute toward Atlanta.

For a seller, the tax side is simple in outline. Property is valued as of January 1, assessed at 40 percent of fair market value, and billed by the tax commissioner at the millage rate set by the local governing bodies. The county's tax commissioner site lays out that sequence, and the sections below cover the Paulding County details that matter when a house changes hands.

sections.h2: Which Paulding County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Two county offices share the work, and a third handles deeds. The Board of Assessors sets values, takes homestead applications and hears the first level of appeals. The tax commissioner bills and collects. The Clerk of Superior Court, in the courthouse, keeps recorded deeds.

Paulding County property tax offices, as listed on the county websites

The commissioner's page warns that the phone line may be cut off early so the office can close at 4:00 p.m. The assessors accept homestead applications by email at the address printed on the county's homestead page, and the board's public meetings run on Wednesdays at 10 a.m. in the third-floor conference room.

sections.h2: When is Paulding County property tax due, and what does a late bill cost?
sections.html:
The commissioner's general information page says property taxes are due by November 15 of each year. A separate FAQ page on the same site still carries a December date for tax year 2024, so read the due date printed on your own bill before you plan a payoff or a closing.

The general information page spells out what happens after the deadline:

  • Interest is added on the 16th of each month at prime plus 3 percent, divided by 12.
  • A lien notice (a FIFA) is filed with the Clerk of Superior Court 30 days after the date on the delinquent notice.
  • A 5 percent penalty is added after 120 days and again every 120 days after that, up to 20 percent.
  • Accounts that stay unpaid are turned over to a contractor, and administrative and levy fees of $215 or more can be added to prepare the parcel for tax sale.

A mobile home follows its own calendar. The county says those bills are usually mailed around January 2 and are due April 1, with a 10 percent penalty added on April 2.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Paulding County assessment?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the mailing date of the assessment notice to appeal, and the county says no appeal can be filed after that window. The appeal can rest on taxability, value or uniformity, and a complaint about the size of the tax bill is not a valid ground.

The path through the system runs in a fixed order:

  • File the appeal with the Board of Assessors, which reviews its own value and tells you what it decided.
  • If no agreement is reached, the appeal goes to the county Board of Equalization, which holds a hearing.
  • You may choose arbitration in place of the Board of Equalization, and the assessors can explain how.
  • If you are still unhappy after that decision, the next step is Superior Court.

The assessors keep an appeals page with a form, a 2026 guide to reading the notice, and a list of 2025 sales used for comparison. If a deployed service member is away, the county says a friend or relative may file within 90 days of the notice of value. Mobile home owners have the same 45 days to declare a different value.

sections.h2: What homestead exemptions can a Paulding County owner claim?
sections.html:
A Paulding County homeowner must apply with the Board of Assessors, because exemptions are never granted automatically. The county asks for proof of residency and citizenship, such as a Georgia driver's license or identification card, and the applicant's name must appear on the deed. You can claim a homestead on only one property, including property in other counties or states.

The county's homestead page names several categories beyond the standard exemption:

  • A school tax exemption for owners age 65 and older.
  • Exemptions for owners who are totally and permanently disabled.
  • An exemption for veterans with a 100 percent service-connected disability.
  • An exemption for the surviving spouse of a peace officer or firefighter killed in the line of duty.
  • An added exemption for homes inside the city limits of Hiram, approved by that city's voters in 2017.

Eligibility turns on owning and occupying the home on January 1. The assessors say applications must arrive by April 1, while the homestead page ties the current-year deadline to the appeal deadline on that year's assessment notice, so file as early as you can. A change in ownership, marriage, divorce or death requires a fresh application with the supporting paperwork. Preferential programs for farmland and timber require a covenant of at least 10 years.

sections.h2: What happens to Paulding County property tax when a house sells?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner bills the parcel, not the sale, so any split of the year's tax between buyer and seller is a term of your sale contract that the closing attorney settles at the table.

Before you list, ask the tax commissioner for the amount owed on the parcel and whether any past-due interest, penalty or lien notice has been added. Any open balance is paid out of your proceeds so the buyer receives a clean parcel. If the sale happens after a November due date but before the bill is paid, confirm in writing who pays it.

After closing, the new owner should make a fresh homestead application, because a change in ownership ends the old one. The seller can notify the assessors that the exemption no longer applies. Deed copies come from the Clerk of Superior Court's deed room in the Paulding County courthouse.

faqs.q: What is the property tax due date in Paulding County?
faqs.a: The commissioner's general information page says November 15 each year. A FAQ page on the same site mentions a December date for tax year 2024, so rely on the date printed on your current bill.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Paulding County property value?
faqs.a: Call the Board of Assessors at 770-443-7606. The tax commissioner at (770) 443-7581 handles billing, payments and payoff figures, not values.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal in Paulding County?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the mailing date of the assessment notice. The county states that appeals cannot be filed after that period ends.

faqs.q: Does Paulding County homestead exemption renew by itself?
faqs.a: Yes, once granted it renews each year unless the owner changes residence, ownership, or seeks a different exemption. A new buyer has to apply again after a sale.

faqs.q: What does Paulding County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: Interest accrues monthly at prime plus 3 percent divided by 12, and a 5 percent penalty is added after 120 days, repeating every 120 days to a 20 percent cap.
